THIS CRIMINAL MISC. CASE HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 18.09.2023, ALONG WITH Crl.MC.7426/2023, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
 Crl.MC Nos.7426 and 7446 of 2023  4  ORDER
The petitioner is common in these cases.

He is the accused in Crime No.165 of 2021 of Kalamassery Police Station, Ernakulam and in Crime No.219 of 2021of Ernakulam South Police Station,
Ernakulam.
Crime No.219 of 2021 has been registered, alleging commission of offences under Sections 354, 506, 294(b) and 34 of the Indian Penal Code and 67A of the Information Technology Act.
The matter is now pending as C.C.No.605 of 2022 on the file of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court (Economic Offences), Ernakulam.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court (Economic Offences), Ernakulam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In Crime No.165 of 2021 of Kalamassery Police Station, Ernakulam, the petitioner faces allegation of having committed the offence under Section 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code.
That case is now pending as S.C.No.389 of 2022 on the file of the Special Court for Trial of Offences against Women and Children, Ernakulam.

entities.text: Special Court for Trial of Offences against Women and Children, Ernakulam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: These petitions under Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure have been filed to quash the proceedings against the petitioner on the ground of settlement of all issues with the third respondent, who is the alleged victim in both the crimes registered against the petitioner.
Crl.MC Nos.7426 and 7446 of 2023 2.
The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner is a 24 years old boy, who was in a relationship with the victim, who is aged 22 years.
It is submitted that, even according to the statement given by the victim/third respondent, the petitioner and the victim were in a relationship.

It is submitted that there is no element of rape or outraging of the modesty of the victim/third respondent by the petitioner and that the entire relationship between the petitioner and the third respondent was purely consensual.

It is submitted that, in the light of the law laid on by this Court in Vishnu V. State of Kerala, [2023 (4) KHC 1] when the entire issues between the petitioner and the third respondent have been settled, the proceedings against the petitioner can be quashed in exercise of the jurisdiction vested in this Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
3.

entities.text: Vishnu V. State of Kerala, [2023 (4) KHC 1]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel appearing for the third respondent would submit that the marriage of the third respondent has now been fixed with another person and she does not intend to continue with the prosecution against the petitioner in any manner.
Crl.MC Nos.7426 and 7446 of 2023 4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned Public Prosecutor and also the learned counsel appearing for the third respondent.

5. A reading of the statement of the third respondent confirmed under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. as well as the final report in crime No.165 of 2021 indicate that the petitioner and the third respondent had entered into the relationship on the promise of marriage.
However, due to some irreconcilable differences, it appears that the petitioner and the third respondent have now decided to part ways.

sentences.text:
In Vishnu (supra), this Court held as follows;
"Similarly, if the allegations and materials disclose that the victim agreed to have sexual intercourse on account of her love and passion for the accused or where the accused could not marry her on account of circumstances beyond his control, the offence will not be attracted.

In these types of cases, there is no point in not exercising the jurisdiction under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. to quash the proceedings on the ground of compromise between the accused and the sexual assault victim".
In such circumstances, I am of the view that the proceedings against the petitioner in both the cases referred to above can be quashed on the ground of settlement.
Therefore, Crl.MC Nos.7426 and 7446 of 2023 these petitions are allowed and

all further proceedings against the petitioner in C.C.No.605 of 2022 on the file of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court (Economic Offences),
Ernakulam and S.C.No.389 of 2022 on the file of the Special Court for Trial of Offences against Women and Children, Ernakulam will stand quashed on the ground of settlement and in the light of the principles laid down in Vishnu (supra).
Sd/-
